title: The two days that started the war

lines.vo: In the summer of 1939 Europe had been at peace for twenty years.
lines.image: a political map of Europe, edge to edge

shot.signature: the camera opens OUT off the map — we start close on one country and pull back until the whole continent is in frame, which is the only shot in the reel that gets wider

layers.prompt: a printed political map of Europe in 1939, muted paper, no text overlay

lines.vo: On the first of September, German tanks crossed the Polish border.
lines.image: a raised wooden border barrier on an empty road

shot.signature: a tank enters from the LEFT and keeps coming while the camera pushes the other way — the one shot where something moves across the frame rather than into it

layers.prompt: an empty country road at a raised border barrier, 1939, overcast
one single 1939 German light tank in strict side profile, whole vehicle in frame, plain white background

lines.vo: Britain and France gave Berlin two days to pull them back.
lines.image: a bare desk under a window

shot.signature: two documents land on the desk from OPPOSITE edges a second apart — one capital, then the other, answering

layers.prompt: a dark wooden desk surface seen straight down, even light, no objects

lines.vo: No answer came. The ultimatum ran out at eleven in the morning.

shot.signature: we fly into the clock and a circle draws itself round the hands as we land on eleven

layers.prompt: a plain plaster wall, even overcast light, nothing on it
a public clock face reading eleven o'clock, 1930s, plain dial

lines.vo: By that evening two empires were at war with Germany.
lines.image: a newspaper seller's stand at dusk
lines.title: AT WAR

shot.signature: the front page fills the whole frame and lands hard — the headline IS the shot, and the street behind it never gets a look in

layers.prompt: a city street at dusk in 1939, wet pavement, low light, empty

lines.vo: Six years later, sixty million people were dead.
lines.title: SIXTY MILLION

shot.signature: the verdict on a hard card with nothing behind it — the number arrives and the reel stops
